ArchitectureNotes.objective: Define VIBE as a graph-first methodology and vibestart as its optional bootstrap/runtime product without collapsing methodology, runtime state, and policy tuning into one surface.
ArchitectureNotes.non-goal: Do not implement the full vibestart deep integration layer in this planning pass.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-1: Overfitting the framework to one agent shell or one product surface would break the agent-agnostic goal.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-2: Allowing prose side-docs to become canonical would create a second knowledge system and accelerate drift.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-3: Letting policy and runtime state mix would turn configuration into an unreadable operational dump.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-4: Allowing implicit routing or projection semantics to remain heuristic would make the anti-drift claim non-reproducible across runtimes.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-5: Using one sync action for both canonical reconciliation and operational cleanup would couple transactions with different safety properties.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-6: Letting a GRACE compatibility shim silently become a new VIBE core source of truth would reintroduce artifact drift through boundary confusion.

contract.purpose: Define VIBE positioning, principles, boundaries, and the relationship to vibestart.

export-identity.PURPOSE: Publish the stable VIBE and vibestart story.

notes.note-1: Must keep GRACE lineage in credits and compatibility, not in the primary value pitch.
notes.note-2: docs/technology.xml may exist for GRACE compatibility, but it must not redefine the canonical VIBE core surfaces.

contract.purpose: Define the graph-first ontology and the semantic invariants that constrain projection into requirements, plan, verification, and decisions.

export-ontology.PURPOSE: Specify node types, stages, edges, and the semantic invariants required for deterministic projection.

notes.note-1: knowledge-graph.xml must stay primary; requirements.xml is a cleaned projection, not the birthplace of ideas.
notes.note-2: The ontology owns projection invariants and maturity semantics; the macro layer owns executable projection controls.

contract.purpose: Define the public macro API as deterministic state machines with routing guards, executable projection controls, read/write sets, invariants, and the internal skill layer that realizes it.

export-macroVocabulary.PURPOSE: Expose discover, refine, deliver, fix, sync, resume, deploy, vibe, and calibrate semantics.

notes.note-1: Compatibility must be preserved at macro semantics and artifact discipline level, not at old command-name level.
notes.note-2: Macro transitions, route selection, and executable projection controls must be formal contracts, not only narrative hints.

contract.purpose: Define adaptive governance as a deterministic review-selection and sync-selection algebra with explicit calibration hooks.

export-governance.PURPOSE: Explain what signals exist and how project thresholds tune them.

notes.note-1: Time is explicitly not a primary governance signal.
notes.note-2: Governance must define precedence, tie-breaking, and unknown-signal behavior so the same observable state yields the same review floor.
notes.note-3: sync must separate reconcile from cleanup and must never mutate unknown artifacts during cleanup.
notes.note-4: fix must support review-after-fix as an adaptive post-repair control hook before the repair is considered closed.

contract.purpose: Define the boundary between vibe.toml, docs/vibe/*.toml, and .vibestart/state/*, including normative defaults and experimental surfaces.

export-configLayout.PURPOSE: Keep active config readable and runtime exhaust isolated.

notes.note-1: Config must remain explanatory and heavily commented.
notes.note-2: guided and single remain normative defaults; auto, multi, and calibrate apply are controlled experimental surfaces until stronger guards exist.
notes.note-3: docs/technology.xml is allowed as a GRACE compatibility shim and remains non-canonical for VIBE core semantics.

contract.purpose: Map the vibestart product to explicit core and deep bootstrap profiles, onboarding flow, and a deterministic first-run contract without making vibestart mandatory for VIBE adoption.

export-bootstrapProfiles.PURPOSE: Expose vibestart core and vibestart deep as explicit setup choices.

export-firstRunContract.PURPOSE: Explain install results, defaults, optionals, and next-step behavior deterministically.

notes.note-1: core and deep are product profiles, not separate methodologies.
notes.note-2: The first-run contract must say what was installed, what defaults are active, what remains optional, and how plain requests will be routed.
notes.note-3: Contract markup and structural labels stay in English even when surrounding explanatory prose may vary by locale.

DF-001.NAME: RawIntentToKnowledge
DF-001.step-1: Capture a new or changed idea as an intent, feature, or work node in the knowledge graph.
DF-001.step-2: Link the new node to existing product and project knowledge.
DF-001.step-3: Promote the node from captured toward clarified or designed when the context is sufficient.
DF-001.evidence: Updated graph node state plus a deterministic route trace that explains why the next step is refine, deliver, or sync.

DF-002.NAME: KnowledgeToExecution
DF-002.step-1: Read clarified or designed nodes from the knowledge graph.
DF-002.step-2: Project stable intent into requirements and executable work into the development and verification plans through deterministic and idempotent projection rules.
DF-002.step-3: Link modules, verification refs, decisions, and deploy concerns back into the graph.
DF-002.evidence: Projection decisions, plan modules, implementation phases, and verification refs linked back to graph nodes.

DF-003.NAME: ExecutionToCoherence
DF-003.step-1: Implement or repair the approved scope under macro and governance rules.
DF-003.step-2: Run verification and the selected review level.
DF-003.step-3: Run sync-reconcile when the policy detects or anticipates drift, then run sync-cleanup only for VIBE-owned operational exhaust.
DF-003.evidence: Code, verification evidence, review result, reconcile deltas, and optional cleanup report.

DF-004.NAME: BootstrapToAdoption
DF-004.step-2: Install canonical VIBE artifacts and policy surfaces.
DF-004.step-3: Apply profile-specific product behavior without changing framework semantics.
DF-004.step-4: Emit a deterministic first-run contract that explains the installed surfaces, defaults, optionals, and next step.
DF-004.evidence: Profile selection, generated files, active defaults, optional surfaces, and an onboarding/first-run trace.

Phase-1.name: Framework Foundation
Phase-1.goal: Lock the identity, ontology, and configuration boundaries before deeper product work begins.
Phase-1.step-1: Define framework identity, principles, and value boundaries.
Phase-1.step-2: Define the graph-first ontology and artifact projection algebra.
Phase-1.step-3: Define the manifest and policy boundary between root config, docs config, and runtime state.

Phase-2.name: Workflow Language
Phase-2.goal: Lock the public macro API and the first governance semantics.
Phase-2.step-1: Define macro contracts, routing guards, and state-machine transitions.
Phase-2.step-2: Define adaptive governance algebra, sync split, thresholds, and calibration hooks.

Phase-3.name: Bootstrap Product Mapping
Phase-3.goal: Map the framework cleanly onto vibestart core and deep profiles.
Phase-3.step-1: Translate the framework surfaces into an explicit bootstrap product contract.

ExecutionPolicy.experimental-guard: Experimental surfaces are allowed but non-normative until deterministic guards and stronger verification are in place.
ExecutionPolicy.controller-owns: docs/requirements.xml, docs/development-plan.xml, docs/verification-plan.xml, docs/knowledge-graph.xml, docs/decisions.xml, docs/technology.xml, vibe.toml, docs/vibe/*.toml
ExecutionPolicy.worker-owns: Scoped implementation surfaces inside the approved write scope; no worker owns the canonical shared artifacts globally.
